Kerr, Newell, Davies, Walker, Black, Dabbs, Linstead, Maclean. How's that for a line up to set a new 3 mile record?

Our turnout for this fixture against Mitcham A.C. and Croydon H. was most disappointing for, besides having a team performing in the Hogs Back race, we were also without the services of Kerr, Dabbs, and Linstead who were unfortunately unavailable.

Worrall won the second string in 51.5 (probably 'niggled' at not being selected as No. 1.) Couzens won the Javelin (155'.1"), Kerr won the mile (4:18.1) and Mike Smithers popped up in several spots to collect valuable points.

Although the winner finished over a minute ahead of the field, the race was full of interest throughout and many observers were speculating as to the humdinger that would ensue if the absent Kerr and Newell were able to get amongst 'this lot'.

Cliff's 5th place was most noteworthy for he seemed to have greater difficulty with the conditions than anyone----conditions that caused several retirements including Kerr, Bradley and O'Hara; although the latter went off course when in the first six.
You will see from the list of Club records shown on pages 21 & 22 that new marks have been set up by our middle-distance men Cocks, Robinson, Kerr and Gerry North.

Gerry North was after Mal Robinson's Championship record of 4:15:8, but with Thresher and Kerr competing in the South v Midlands v North match at Wolverhampton he had to run solo for the final two laps.
With the absence of our best three runners of the moment---Gerry North, Kerr and Thresher---it was very encouraging to see such excellent running from the first four finishers.
A disappointing championship with 9 retirements, including Kerr, Hart and Pat Newell. Gerry North moved away in the latter stages of the race, doing just enough to win.

Belgrave won the 2 miles team race with John Thresher the winner in 9:09 supported by Gerry North (9:20) and John Bicourt (9:28). Kerr and O'Hara took the 'A' and 'B' miles with 4:20:0 and 4:20:4 respectively.
Despite being without Gerry North, Thresher and Kerr our team still shook Portsmouth to the core over this course of six long and six short stages run alternately.
SURREY: Gerry North, Thresher, Fairclough, Steer, Dabbs, Black. MIDDLESEX: Hart, O'Hara, Kerr, Newell, Dear and Crookes. What a pity that Geoff North, Thorpe, Barrow and Brown qualify for neither!
With Gerry North, Thresher and Barrow not running (besides other possibles like Newell, Reilly, Dance and Kerr) this surely would have produced our fastest "Brighton" team.
Kerr, Linstead and Dear were capable of causing some upsets. The biggest surprise though, in the end, was Geoff's state of fitness which gave him the slowest time in our 'A' and 'B' teams.

Well, I believe it will be Belgrave if the following team is turned out;- LONG STAGES: Gerry North, Fairclough, Thresher, Barrow, Hart, Kerr,. SHORT STAGES: Geoff North, O'Hara, Williams, Bicourt, Dance, Major,.
Major issues in the middle distance such as O'HARA, BUXTON And KERR have slipped a few seconds whilst NORTH industries are experiencing injuries and do not at present inspire a buyers market.

Agreed that the North brothers, Dance, Whewell, Williams, Kerr and others have played parts of varying degrees in our success but they joined us on moving to London because they had to change their club.

Gilt edge Hart, Duquemin, Middleton, Major, Kerr and Martin continue as the backbone of our economy. Whilst high flyers Bent and Thresher continue to excite, Dull spots occurred with results from Hilton, C.
For the short legs Hart, O'Connor, Dance and Diprose look well placed, with the last two places to be scrambled for by Bicourt, O'Hara, Piotrowski, Cross and Kerr.

Satchell, Walker, Kerr and Black who were still on a grand tour of the Surrey roads when the starting pistol was fired. Bad luck of course but one would expect to find experienced runners acquainting themselves with the course a good half hour before the start.

Kerr and Mann were pushing the early pace with O'Hara, Piotrowski, Fairclough and Major tagging along. The last two named lost contact at about 3,000 metres but the situation ahead of them took a dramatic turn at 5,000 metres when Piotrowski retired with a blistered foot.

It coincides with the running into form, just at the right time, of Kerr, Thresher, North, Major and Fairclough. With Bicourt and Hart already in fine fettle we could well be having a celebration dip in the Lido on September 12th.

Phil' Idowu, Austin Ferns, Marlon Dickson, Chris' Lambert, Marlon Kerr, Charles Igbon, Samson Oni, Matt' Russell, Darren Thompson... All of these and more athletes have enjoyed regular appearances in our showcase team either in League or Cup contests.
